resources.string: How the gluteus maximus extends the hip
Simplified side views with the front of the body to the right. The blue arcs indicate hip motion, not measured angles or muscle force.

The gluteus maximus spans from the back of the pelvis across the back of the hip. Its lower attachments include the upper femur and tissues along the outer thigh. This view highlights the femoral attachment.
The thigh moves on the pelvis
With the pelvis shown still, the femur moves backward relative to it about the center of the hip. The gluteus maximus contributes to this hip extension. The pale outline shows the starting position.
The pelvis moves on the thigh

With the femur held still in this view, the pelvis rotates back around the same hip center. The lower spine moves with the pelvis here without changing its own curve. The hip extends in this view too.
Hip extension is not spinal extension

On the left, the angle between the pelvis and femur changes. On the right, the lumbar spine extends while the hip angle stays the same. Both motions can occur together, but they are not the same joint action.
